key_insight: Mesh-based graph neural networks incorporate neighboring flow information, improving on purely local closure predictions in periodic-hills tests.
engineering_relevance: Non-local learned closures could improve RANS turbulence modeling by exploiting the connectivity already available in finite-volume meshes.
method: Represent finite-volume cells as nodes and shared faces as graph edges.
Use GCN message passing so k layers access each cell’s k-hop neighborhood.
Train on breadth-first-search k-hop subgraphs to augment data and reduce per-graph cost.
evidence_signal: Against equal-size feed-forward networks, GCNs generalized better in a laminar transport benchmark and delivered modest, consistent eddy-viscosity prediction improvements on Closure Challenge periodic-hills data at Re = 5600.
watch_item: The turbulent results remain a proof of concept; broader flow generalization and performance within coupled RANS simulations are not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Graph Neural Network based non-local models: Toward application to RANS turbulence modeling
